Title: Diagnosis of test `testEscapeJavaWithSlash`

Details:
The test `testEscapeJavaWithSlash` checks that the method `StringEscapeUtils.escapeJava(String)` does not escape the forward slash character `/`. The test input is `"String with a slash (/) in it"`, and the expected output is the input string unchanged. The test fails because the actual output escapes the slash character as `\/`.

From the inspected code:
- The method `escapeJava(String)` calls `escapeJavaStyleString(str, false)`.
- The `escapeJavaStyleString(String, boolean)` method uses a `StringWriter` and calls `escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean)`.
- The core logic is in `escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean)`.
- Inside this method, characters in the string are processed one by one.
- For each character `ch` less than 0x7f, a switch case handles:
  - `'` (single quote)
  - `"` (double quote)
  - `\\` (backslash)
  - `/` (slash)
  - other characters

Specifically, when the character is a slash (`case '/'` at line 243), the method writes a backslash `\\` first (`out.write('\\')` at line 244), then writes the slash character itself (`out.write('/')` at line 245).

This means the slash character is being escaped to `\/`. However, from the test comment, escaping slashes is not valid in Java strings and should not be done.

Hence, the bug is that the `escapeJavaStyleString` method unnecessarily escapes the slash `/` character, causing the test to fail as it expects the slash not to be escaped but it is.

The bug occurs because in the switch section that handles characters less than 0x7f, the slash character case escapes it when it should simply output the slash character as is.

Suggested location(s) to fix:
- `org.apache.commons.lang.StringEscapeUtils.escapeJavaStyleString(java.io.Writer,java.lang.String,boolean)`

The fix would be to remove or comment out the line which writes the backslash before the slash, i.e., remove `out.write('\\');` at line 244 in the slash case.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
